claims.text: Atomic-level lattice strain governs the onset of premelting in HEA nanoparticles.
Atomic-level lattice strain governs the overall melting temperature of HEA nanoparticles.
Size and bonding mismatch among multiple constituent elements produces local lattice strain.
Local lattice strain produces a heterogeneous distribution of bond strengths within an HEA nanoparticle.
Highly strained regions have weakened bonds and therefore initiate premelting.
Premelting preferentially begins at the nanoparticle surface or other regions of enhanced strain.
Less-strained, strongly bonded interior regions delay complete melting.
Configurational entropy stabilizes the single-phase state and contributes to the overall melting behavior.
HEA nanoparticles undergo surface premelting below the corresponding bulk melting point.
The overall melting temperature of HEA nanoparticles exceeds the weighted average of the melting points of their constituent elements.
Single-component or low-entropy nanoparticles of comparable size melt more uniformly than HEA nanoparticles.
Low-entropy alloy nanoparticles have melting points closer to a simple average of their constituent melting points than HEA nanoparticles do.
Matched single-metal or low-entropy nanoparticles will lack the pronounced surface premelting expected in HEA nanoparticles.
Matched single-metal or low-entropy nanoparticles will lack the elevated melting temperature expected in HEA nanoparticles.
The proposed strain-controlled behavior should hold for homogeneously mixed HEA nanoparticles approximately 20–100 nm in diameter.
HEA nanoparticles smaller than approximately 20 nm may deviate from the predicted melting behavior.
Significant phase segregation or chemical short-range order can alter the local strain distribution and cause deviations from the predicted melting behavior.
Changing HEA composition can tune the expected lattice strain.
